players.product: superconducting QPUs made in its own Fab-1 (84-qubit Ankaa-3 on Amazon Braket, 36-qubit Cepheus-1-36Q chiplet system, 9-qubit Novera on-premises QPU)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Subodh Kulkarni: under the letter of intent announced May 21, the U.S. Department of Commerce selected Rigetti for a potential award of up to $100 million in funding over three years to accelerate superconducting quantum computing R&D on key scaling challenges; the funding would be allocated under the CHIPS Research and Development Office broad agency announcement pursuant to the CHIPS Act, and the contemplated structure includes the Department receiving an equity stake in Rigetti. CFO Jeff Bertelsen: should the LOI move to definitive agreements, Rigetti expects to deploy the funding on specific technical programs that address scaling bottlenecks and packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: up to $100 million over three years (Department of Commerce LOI, CHIPS R&D)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jeff Bertelsen: Rigetti ended Q2 2026 with approximately $541.3 million in cash, cash equivalents and available-for-sale investments (March 31, 2026: $569 million; December 31, 2025: $589.8 million) and continues to operate with no debt.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$541.3 million (vs $569 million at March 31, 2026); no debt
